desc:
You are given a string s and a list of queries. Each query is a pair [l, r] (0-indexed, both ends inclusive) that selects the substring s[l..r]. For every query, answer 1 if the selected substring is a palindrome and 0 otherwise.

Return the answers as an array in the order of the queries.

For example, for s = "abacaba" and the queries [0,6], [1,3], [2,4], [3,3], [0,2], [1,4] the answer is [1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0].
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
0 ≤ l ≤ r < s.length for every query
hints: Checking each query directly by comparing characters costs O(length) per query, which can be slow for many long queries. Preprocess the string once.
Every palindrome is centered at a letter (odd length) or between two letters (even length). For each center, how far does the palindrome extend?

Compute the maximal radius around every center (Manacher's algorithm, or expand around each center in O(n2) total). The query [l, r] is a palindrome exactly when the center at l + r reaches at least r - l + 1 letters.
editorial: If a substring is a palindrome, so is the substring obtained by trimming one letter from each end. So for each center it is enough to know the length of the longest palindrome around it: every shorter palindrome with the same center exists too, and nothing longer does.

Insert a separator between all letters (#a#b#a#) so that odd and even centers are treated alike, and compute p[c], the length of the longest palindrome of the original string centered at c, with Manacher's algorithm in O(n). The substring s[l..r] has its center at index l + r + 2 in the padded string ^#s0#s1#...#$, so the answer to a query is 1 if p[l + r + 2] ≥ r - l + 1.
Preprocessing is O(n), every query is O(1), so the total is O(n + q). A simple alternative is to build the boolean table pal[i][j] in O(n2) time and memory.
